prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision: Build a fair, free and open society by widening opportunity, sharing power, and balancing liberty, equality and community. Active, enabling government should invest in people, spread power locally, protect the environment, and be accountable.

Education (flagship):
- Invest £2bn/year funded by 1p on basic income tax.
- Universal high‑quality early years for all 3–4 year‑olds; scrap nursery vouchers.
- Double spending on books/equipment year one; tackle school repairs (£500m/5 years).
- Cut primary class sizes so no 5–11 year‑old is in a class over 30 within 5 years.
- General Teaching Council; stronger inspection; anti‑bullying/truancy drive.
- Replace National Curriculum with a focused Minimum Curriculum Entitlement.
- Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; 2% remissible training levy on firms (SMEs exempt); expand youth training; Quality Council for post‑16.

Economy and enterprise:
- Stability: independent UK Reserve Bank; adhere to “golden rule” (borrow only to invest).
- Euro: join if Maastricht criteria met and approved by referendum.
- Shift tax from jobs/consumption to pollution; promote saving.
- SMEs: tackle late payment, cut red tape, expand finance, fairer local business rating long‑term.
- Regional Development Agencies; boost R&D; stronger competition law; reform utility regulation under a single consumer‑focused regulator.

Environment and transport:
- Embed sustainability across government; annual PM report on targets.
- Cut CO₂ 30% from 1990 levels over 15 years; green tax shift including phased carbon tax offset by NI/VAT cuts.
- Major public transport investment; enable urban road pricing hypothecated to transit; keep London Underground public; treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010; stronger rail regulation; incentives for fuel‑efficient cars (lower VED, higher fuel duty).
- National home insulation programme starting with 2m lowest‑income households; promote renewables; no new nuclear subsidies; do not replace nuclear at end of life.
- Stronger water, countryside and planning protections; product reuse/recycling incentives; robust animal welfare (ban cosmetic testing; free vote on hunting).

Safer communities and housing:
- 3,000 more police; reduce paperwork; focus on prevention, restorative justice, youth interventions; drugs Royal Commission; better victim support; accountable London police authority.
- Housing: build via public‑private‑housing association partnerships; release council house receipts; new Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers; end rough sleeping by 2000; bring empty homes into use; fair, secure renting.

NHS and care:
- Extra £540m/year (funded by ending NI perks loophole and +5p on cigarettes).
- Freeze prescription charges; restore free eye/dental checks.
- Six‑month moratorium on finance‑driven closures; cut waits to max 6 months in 3 years.
- End two‑tier GP fundholding; National Inspectorate for Health & Social Care.
- Recruit for frontline care (e.g., 10,000 nurses/5,000 doctors equivalent).
- Community care: stronger standards, Carer’s Benefit, more choice and respite.

Constitution and rights:
- Incorporate ECHR; Bill of Rights; Freedom of Information; cut quangos; wider use of referendums.
- Electoral reform: PR for all elections; reduce MPs by ~200; predominantly elected second chamber; fixed four‑year terms; party funding transparency/limits.
- Devolution: Home Rule for Scotland and Wales (PR, tax‑varying powers); English regional assemblies by demand; stronger local government; long‑term Local Income Tax and fairer business rates.

Welfare, equality, families:
- Break poverty trap: raise tax thresholds; new 50p rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with simpler Low Income Benefit; benefit‑to‑work transfers for long‑term unemployed; childcare strategy; regionally‑set minimum wage; tackle fraud/evasion.
- Older people: earnings‑linked top‑up to guarantee minimum income; flexible retirement 60–70; move from contributory pensions to residence‑based; expand portable private/occupational pensions.
- Youth: restore benefits for 16–17s; Citizens Service; citizenship education; statutory youth services.
- Women, disabled, ethnic minorities, LGBT+: stronger anti‑discrimination, equal workplace rights (including part‑time), disability civil rights, fair policing, equal age of consent, repeal Section 28.

Foreign policy, defence, development:
- Positive EU leadership; democratise EU; PR for MEPs 1999; conditional euro entry by referendum; reform CAP/CFP; enhance EU justice co‑operation with safeguards.
- Maintain defence capability; retain Trident with capped warheads; support NATO enlargement; advance arms control (CTBT).
- UN reform: stronger peacekeeping, ICC; global environmental leadership; aid to reach 0.7% GNP within 10 years; debt relief; end tied aid; strict arms export controls; ban landmines; fair trade with labour/environment standards.

Tax contract: transparency, costed pledges, waste reduction first, fairness. 70% pay lower or unchanged tax; ~500,000 lifted out of tax; most taxpayers pay about 45p/week extra excluding top earners.
